title: Slimline Sparkband: guided interaction and accessible degradation for high-density time-series
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: Our existing time-series legend and tooltip patterns create large DOM payloads and cognitive overload on small viewports. High-card dashboards with 20+ series cause jank and tabbing becomes noisy for screen reader users. Proposal: introduce a compact 'Slimline Sparkband' representation that replaces full legend rows with micro-sparklines + condensed labels and an affordance for expanding to full details. Provide an ARIA-first degradation pattern so screen readers receive meaningful summaries without iterating 20+ items. This ticket covers the design prototype, acceptance criteria, and handoff notes for engineering implementation (virtualized list, canvas fallback, aria-live summarizer, and tokenized spacing rules).
acceptance_criteria: Designs for collapsed and expanded states of Slimline Sparkband created and approved in Figma
ARIA strategy documented: non-interactive summary announced on load, expansion focusable, keyboard support for expand/collapse
Performance budget documented: legend DOM node count reduced by >=70% on dashboards with 20+ series
Prototype demonstrates canvas fallback for <2W GPU scenarios and virtualized list in React for legend expansion
Design tokens for spacing, color contrast, and micro-sparkline stroke width added to token spec
Cross-browser keyboard and screen-reader QA checklist completed and linked
Hand-off notes and engineering acceptance tests added to the PR before merging
dev_notes: Prefer canvas-rendered micro-sparklines inside a virtualized legend row to reduce DOM pressure.
Event delegation: single pointer listener on legend container; avoid per-item listeners.
ARIA approach: provide an aria-live polite region with a short summary string like 'Showing 12 series; 3 have recent alerts; press E to expand legend'.
Keyboard support: Tab should land on the expand affordance; Enter/Space toggles expanded view; Up/Down arrow navigates expanded items.
Fallbacks: on low-GPU or server-side-rendered pages, render simplified SVG sparklines with limited ticks and a no-animation flag.
Metrics: measure initial paint time for legend, time to interactive for legend affordance, and DOM node count before and after change.
Suggested feature flag name: charts.slimline_sparkband_v1 for staged rollout.

qa_steps: Load sample dashboard with 24 series and record initial legend DOM node count and TTI.
Toggle Slimline Sparkband collapsed -> expanded and verify focus moves to first expanded item.
Screen reader pass: NVDA and VoiceOver should receive the short summary on page load and should not iterate through 20+ legend items unless expanded.
Keyboard navigation: ensure Expand control reachable via Tab, Enter/Space toggles expansion, arrow keys navigate when expanded.
Visual regression: verify contrast ratios for condensed labels and sparkline strokes meet AA guidelines.
Performance regression: compare dashboard render time and memory usage before and after change; target >= 40% reduction in legend-related layout cost.
